key_insight: Mixing near no-slip stagnation points on solid boundaries follows a universal two-regime law: fluid stretching dominates early, then boundary-diffusion coupling sets a new Pe^{-1/3} mixing scale and exponential decay.
engineering_relevance: This gives a predictive rule for scalar transport near obstacles in porous media and other wall-bounded flows, helping estimate when diffusion at solid surfaces will control contamination or reactant homogenization.
method: Analyze thin solute strips/sheets near separatrices ending at stagnation points.
Derive asymptotic scalar concentration and width laws by coupling advection with diffusion near the wall.
Validate the theory with numerical simulations and identify the crossover time t_B ~ Pe^{1/3}.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a complete analytical theory that is validated by numerical simulations, with asymptotic scalings for c_max(t), sigma(t), and the crossover time t_B.
watch_item: The results are specific to idealized thin blobs near generic no-slip stagnation points, so applying them to complex geometries or strongly time-dependent flows may require caution.
paper_title: Scalar mixing by stagnation points on solid surfaces
